geometry.coordinate: x=0 bottom face; x=L top face; cell-centred finite volumes
geometry.status: Inherited bounded equivalent thickness, not a complete as-built deck/concrete assembly.

constant_properties.status: Unchanged V11J verification constants; not calibrated WTC slab properties.

surface_exchange.stefan_boltzmann_status: 2022 CODATA/NIST value; exact under the 2019 SI because k, h and c are exact.
surface_exchange.coefficient_status: All h, emissivity, gas-temperature and radiative-temperature values in the six cases are synthetic verification parameters, not inferred WTC exposures.

numerical_method.scheme: Backward Euler in time and conservative cell-centred finite volumes in space. A Newton solve couples both massless nonlinear surface balances to the conduction cells; the tridiagonal Jacobian includes exact boundary derivatives.
numerical_method.absolute_temperature_policy: Radiation powers use kelvins after adding exactly 273.15; convection and conduction use temperature differences, for which degC and K increments are identical.

scope.domain: One square metre, one-dimensional coordinate x from the idealized slab bottom face x=0 to the top face x=L. Constant k, rho and cp inherited unchanged from V11J.
scope.surface_boundary: Each massless surface satisfies conduction through the adjacent half cell equals convection plus long-wave radiation into the coupon. Gas and radiative temperatures are synthetic verification inputs.
scope.sign_convention: Every reported boundary component is positive into the coupon. At every face q_in=q_conv_in+q_rad_in=2*k*(T_surface-T_adjacent_cell)/dx.
scope.coupling_policy: The calculated fields remain outside V11I. They are not panel loads, fire histories, WTC gas temperatures, mechanical states or evidence of collapse.
scope.history_policy: No V11E/V11F/V11H/V11I damage variable, stress state, material property or energy ledger is edited. The V11J constant-property results are a saved hash control, not re-executed.
scope.energy_policy: For unit area, sensible enthalpy change equals the time integral of bottom and top convective plus radiative heat. Surface storage is zero. Global collapse-energy credit is exactly zero.

method_sources.scope: Primary NIST guidance states the simple convection relation Qc=h*As*(Ts-Tf), notes typical fire-compartment h values of about 10 to 30 W/(m2 K), and treats convection plus radiation as the surface boundary for conduction. V11K reverses the sign to report heat into the coupon.

Primary NIST FDS technical reference describes net solid-surface heat flux as convective plus radiative contributions and couples it to one-dimensional solid conduction. V11K uses only the stated idealized boundary structure, not an FDS fire field.
Primary NIST constants table gives sigma=5.670374419...e-8 W m-2 K-4, exact in the 2019 SI.
